slides.text: I clean up the messes the city's worst criminals leave behind. Blood, bone, teeth—I bleach it all away for ten thousand dollars a job, no questions asked. Tonight’s address was a luxurious penthouse downtown. The client’s instructions were standard: eliminate the mess in the master bathroom, dispose of the body, leave no trace. But when I unzipped the thick plastic body bag to apply the dissolving agent, my heart completely stopped.

The dead man staring back at me was a stranger, but he was wearing my husband Mark's wedding ring and his custom tailored suit. Confused, I searched the dead man's pockets. I found a burner phone and a folded piece of paper. The paper was a hit contract. The target wasn't the man in the bag. The target was me. And the signature at the bottom of the contract belonged to Mark.

I unlocked the burner phone. The last message received sent a chill down my spine: 'Dummy body is in place. The cleaner will arrive at 2 AM. Once she’s locked inside the bathroom, burn the penthouse down.' I lunged for the bathroom door, but the handle wouldn't budge. Smoke was already creeping under the doorframe. Through the thick wood, I heard Mark's muffled voice. 'Till death do us part, darling.'
